fester-huelfskreis.translation: Fixed Auxiliary Circle with Given Center M
fester-huelfskreis.definition: Steiner's single permanent reference circle in the plane. Together with its center M, it supplies an involution of parallel diameters and orthogonal chords enabling pure straightedge simulation of all compass intersections; without M, projective collineations fixing the circle break Euclidean metric structure.

aehnlichkeitspunkte.translation: External and Internal Centers of Similitude (Homothetic Centers)
aehnlichkeitspunkte.definition: In Steiner's Zweites Kapitel (§§ 12–13) and Sechste bis Achte Aufgabe (§ 18), the harmonic centers A and I on the line of centers M M_1 through which parallel radii of the fixed drawn circle M and an un-drawn virtual circle M_1 correspond under straightedge projection.

aehnlichkeitsaxe.definition: A straight line passing through three centers of similitude of three circles taken in pairs; Steiner demonstrates that the six centers of similitude lie three by three on four axes of similitude by straightedge alone.

linie-der-gleichen-potenzen.definition: Coined via Steiner's 'Potenz des Punctes' (1826/1833, §§ 14–17) and Gaultier/Chasles's 'axe radical': the straight locus of points having equal power d_1^2 - r_1^2 = d_2^2 - r_2^2 with respect to two circles, constructed by straightedge alone in Problem 8 to intersect two un-drawn circles.

potenz-eines-punktes.translation: Power of a Point with Respect to a Circle
potenz-eines-punktes.definition: For a point P and circle (M, r) at distance d = PM, the product of secant segments PA · PB = d^2 - r^2; introduced by Steiner in 1826 and fundamental to his theory of radical axes.

punkt-der-gleichen-potenzen.definition: The unique intersection point of the three radical axes of three circles taken in pairs, from which tangents to all three circles have equal length.

harmonische-strahlen.definition: Four concurrent straight lines a, b, c, d whose cross-ratio (a, b; c, d) = -1; every transversal cutting the four rays produces a harmonic range of four collinear points.

harmonische-punkte.definition: Four collinear points A, B, C, D such that the cross-ratio (A, B; C, D) = (CA/CB) / (DA/DB) = -1; C and D divide the segment AB internally and externally in the same ratio.

vollstaendiges-viereck.definition: A configuration of four points (vertices), no three collinear, and the six straight lines joining them; its three diagonal points form a diagonal triangle whose sides divide the opposite vertices harmonically.

vollstaendiges-vierseit.definition: A configuration of four straight lines (sides), no three concurrent, and their six intersection points; dual to the complete quadrangle, its three diagonals form a triangle whose vertices separate the sides harmonically.

pol-und-polare.translation: Pole and Polar with Respect to a Circle
pol-und-polare.definition: The projective relationship where each point P (pole) is paired with a straight line p (polar) such that any secant through P cutting the circle at A, B has its harmonic conjugate on p; Steiner proves that polars can be constructed by straightedge alone.

satz-des-thales.definition: The theorem that an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle; used by Steiner in the Dritte Aufgabe to construct perpendiculars using chords of the fixed circle.

orthocentrum.definition: The common point of concurrency of the three altitudes of a triangle; constructed with straightedge alone on a diameter of the fixed circle to yield exact right angles.

geometrographie-steinerienne.definition: Quantitative operational analysis of constructions executed using only the straightedge (l_1 R_1 + l_2 R_2, circles = 0) with a single fixed circle and its center in the plane.

geometrographie-mascheronienne.definition: Evaluation of constructions restricted exclusively to the compass (m_1 C_1 + m_2 C_2 + m_3 C_3, lines = 0) following Lorenzo Mascheroni (1797).

eichmass.definition: In Hilbert's Grundlagen der Geometrie (§ 36), an instrument capable of laying off a fixed unit segment along any ray; Hilbert proved that straightedge + Eichmaß generates only the pythagorean field, whereas Steiner's drawn circle generates the full Euclidean closure.

steiner-punkt.definition: In triangle geometry, the circumcircle point X(99) discovered by Steiner; in projective geometry, one of the 20 points where three Pascal lines concur, or the two star points S+, S- in the Pappus S_3 configuration.

equerre.definition: Auxiliary drafting triangle slid along a fixed straightedge to draw parallels and perpendiculars directly; first analyzed in Lemoine's 1888 Oran note and formalized in Scientia No. 18 (1902) via elementary alignment and sliding operations.
